It provides a concrete scenario that confirms the slave's behavior aligns with the intended functionality, ensuring that the system does not attempt to re-fetch the entire index when it is not needed. Root cause:
The bug was caused by the Solr slave performing a full replication of the entire index whenever the master Solr instance restarted, regardless of whether the index had changed. This behavior was inappropriate and inefficient, particularly in scenarios where no actual updates had occurred in the index. The root cause is tied to how the replication success state was managed, which did not account for whether the Solr instance was aware of ZooKeeper and did not properly track the replication process in non-ZooKeeper configurations.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
core.getUpdateHandler().getSolrCoreState().setLastReplicateIndexSuccess(successfulInstall);
```
Reason:
This statement indiscriminately sets the last replication success state based on the `successfulInstall` variable without checking if the Solr instance is running in a ZooKeeper-aware mode. As a result, if the master Solr instance restarts, the slave performs a full replication of the entire index regardless of whether there were actual changes, leading to inefficiency.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
if (core.getCoreDescriptor().getCoreContainer().isZooKeeperAware()) {
    // we only track replication success in SolrCloud mode
    core.getUpdateHandler().getSolrCoreState().setLastReplicateIndexSuccess(successfulInstall);
}
```
Reason:
This modification introduces a check to ensure that the replication success state is only updated when the Solr instance is running in ZooKeeper-aware mode. This prevents the slave from unnecessarily performing a full replication when there have been no changes, thus resolving the bug and enhancing efficiency.
